The Danish Institute for Advanced Study (DIAS) and the Department of Technology and Innovation at the University of Southern Denmark (SDU) seek an outstanding candidate to fill a tenure track Fellow (Assistant Professor level) position in the field of Biomedical Engineering. The candidate is expected to start on June 1, 2027, or as soon as possible thereafter. 

We are looking for a researcher with clear potential for research excellence who thrives in and is inspired by interdisciplinary collaboration. The ideal candidate will be expected to contribute to high-quality research in their field while embracing DIAS’s mission of curiosity-driven inquiry and interdisciplinary dialogue. The successful candidate should have a strong and promising research profile, with potential for attracting external research funding, and a demonstrated ability to work across disciplines. The candidate will be attached to both the Department and DIAS and should be prepared to engage in multiple and diverse research environments at SDU. Teaching obligations will be reduced compared to a standard assistant professorship at SDU, allowing more time for research and leadership activities. 

We are looking for a distinguished researcher to take up this position at the newly established Centre of Biomedical Engineering (BEC) at SDU. The ideal candidate has deep knowledge about engineering, physics and maths. They have experience of working with healthcare professionals and are great communicators of complex ideas. The field of biomedical engineering is interpreted in a broad manner. However, there needs to be clear evidence of (potential) clinical translation and stakeholder engagement for patient impact. It is expected that the successful candidate can move from fundamental science to technology readiness level 6 or above. 

We seek a researcher with expertise in the field of biomedical engineering, who is eager to develop their research career within the DIAS framework. The ideal candidate should demonstrate: 

  • A commitment to engaging in boundary-crossing interdisciplinary research and dialogue.

  • A strong commitment to interdisciplinary collaboration, contributing to research that bridges multiple fields. 

  • Strong interest in driving internationally competitive research activities at the highest level of ambition. 

  • Engagement in various forms of research dissemination, including interdisciplinary research and dialogue. 

 

Qualifications

Successful applicants must: 

  • Hold a PhD or similar qualifications within relevant fields of biomedical engineering, computational bioengineering, mechanical or electrical engineering. To qualify for the position as Assistant Professor you must have obtained a PhD or similar degree by the application deadline.  

  • Ability to work well in a team, and coordinate team research.

  • Excellent coding skills and/or exceptional experimental competences.

  • Exhibit curiosity-driven research excellence, thinking beyond traditional boundaries. 

  • Be fluent in English.

  • Show potential for attracting external research funding. Experience in applying for external funding and a strong international network are considered comparative advantages.

  • Have research publications that demonstrate their excellence and broad thinking. 

 

The Danish Institute for Advanced Study (DIAS)

DIAS at SDU is a hub for interdisciplinary excellence at and beyond the frontier of knowledge, bringing together outstanding researchers from various disciplines to foster groundbreaking interdisciplinary research and bold innovation. DIAS nurtures a collaborative and curiosity-driven environment, encouraging scholars to think outside the box and challenge conventional boundaries. The institute values open-minded exploration and an ambitious yet collegial atmosphere with a strong sense of community. Researchers affiliated with DIAS are expected to contribute actively to DIAS activities, and engage in interdisciplinary collaborations across faculties and departments, both nationally and internationally.    

 

Department of Technology and Innovation

The Department of Technology and Innovation is host to research groups that cross domain-specific boundaries to solve complex problems. The Biomedical Engineering Centre (BEC) at the department conducts interdisciplinary research at the interface of biomechanics, sensing, medical devices, and computational modelling. The successful candidate will join a growing research program focused on creating novel medical technologies. 

BEC is committed to developing engineered solutions that are intuitive, practical, and accessible to clinical users. We use a need-driven approach to ensure the technologies we develop are fit for purpose and directly address real clinical challenges. The centre has strong collaborative ties with leading institutions, such as the University of Oxford, and an international outlook is favored by the Department. 

 

Additional information

For further information about being a professor at DIAS, please contact DIAS director Sten Rynning at +45 6550 2193 or via email at director-dias@sdu.dk.

For more questions about the position please contact jberg@iti.sdu.dk (Professor Jeroen Bergmann).

 

Application, salary, and employment terms

The position is based at the Biomedical Engineering Centre in Odense and is also expected to participate DIAS activities and interdisciplinary cooperation in Odense regularly.

Employment is governed by the collective agreement between the Danish Ministry of Finance and the Danish Confederation of Professional Associations (AC) and the provisions for tenure track assistant professor as described herein. Persons employed in the position may, based on a specific individual managerial assessment, be exempted from time registration, also known as a “self-organizer”.

The salary comprises a seniority-based base salary and a centrally agreed supplement.

Additional supplements may be negotiated locally.

As of 1 August 2026, the annual salary for an Assistant Professor is DKK 480,224.96 (salary level 6), consisting of a base salary of DKK 417,456 and a supplement of DKK 62,768.96.

All amounts are stated before tax, before added pension (18.07%), and any additional supplements. Pension contributions are paid by SDU, and both salary components (the annual salary and the supplement) are pensionable. For more details on salary and taxation, please see Further information on salary and taxation.

The tenure track programme is aimed at the most talented scholars who have established a high level in their current research and other professional work, and those who possess exceptional potential to achieve the highest international level within their research area. 

Candidates enter at the assistant professor level (up to six years) and, upon successful completion, will be promoted to a permanent position as associate professor, subject to a positive assessment by an expert committee.  This evaluation is based on an overall assessment of the candidate's academic achievements and potential. 

Indicators of relevant scholarly merits include documented ability to develop an independent and internationally recognized research profile, deliver high-quality teaching and supervision, contribute actively to the academic community, and demonstrate the potential to secure competitive external research funding and build an ambitious research programme. The evaluation may also consider the candidate's contributions to the strategic and organizational development of the department, including a willingness to engage in academic leadership and administrative responsibilities.  

As part of the tenure-track programme, the Assistant Professor is expected to complete SDU's Lecturer Training Programme before the evaluation, unless an equivalent university-level programme has already been completed at another institution.

The programme includes annual performance reviews, a midterm evaluation by an expert panel, and a final academic assessment. If the final assessment is positive, the candidate will progress to a permanent position as associate professor. If the final evaluation is negative, the assistant professor may request one additional assessment within the last six months of employment. The tenure track period may be extended in connection with maternity, paternity, or adoption leave.

 

Application requirementsThe application must include the following:

  • Letter of motivation that clearly explains the applicant's interest, qualifications, and motivation for the position.

  • Detailed CV including documentation of experience, and contacts for possible references. 

  • An elaborated research and funding plan (max 4 pages) for the next three years including a description of synergy with the department's activities and the potential to benefit from DIAS’s interdisciplinary environment.

  • Master’s and PhD degree certificates or equivalent (original and an official English translation).   

  • Complete list of publications, indicating which publications are most relevant for the position.

  • Up to 3 of the most relevant research articles – if you submit a monograph, it counts as 3 articles. Please upload a pdf for each publication. For co-authored publications, briefly describe the extent of the co-authorship or your contribution to the publications (please do this for each co-authored publication). You can do so by using this form or by describing the co-authorship in such a way that the committee can assess the extent of your contribution.

  • Teaching Portfolio as documentation for teaching experience as well as supervision qualifications. Any format is acceptable, but you can find inspiration for structuring your teaching portfolio on the Faculty's teaching portfolio page. 

All application materials must be submitted in English, and only applications written in English will be considered.

We recommend that international applicants take the time to visit websites of Work in Denmark and the International Staff Office at SDU. Here you can find information and facts about moving to, working and living in Denmark.

 

Submission guidelines

  • Motivated application must be uploaded under ‘Cover letter’ (max. 5 MB), Curriculum Vitae must be uploaded under ‘Resume’ (max 5 MB). All other documents must be uploaded under ‘Miscellaneous documents’ (max 10 files with a maximum 50 MB per file).  

  • All files must be submitted in PDF format which must be unlocked, allow binding and may not be password protected. Any CPR number (civil registration number) must be crossed out.  

 

Assessment

Shortlisting may be used as part of the assessment process. Read about shortlisting at SDU.

Assessment of applications will be done under the existing Appointment Order for universities. Applications will be assessed by an assessment committee. The committee may request additional information, and, if so, it is the responsibility of the applicant to provide the necessary material. 

When the assessment committee has submitted its report, the applicant will receive the part of the evaluation that concerns them. 

Applications that are incomplete with regards to the above requirements will not be assessed by the committee. Shortlisting and tests may be used in the assessment process and references may be obtained. 

 

About SDU SDU is committed to fostering a diverse staff that reflects society’s diversity. We welcome applications from all qualified candidates, regardless of personal background. SDU was founded in 1966 and now has over 27,000 students, nearly 20% of whom are international. SDU employs more than 3,800 staff and offers 115 study programmes across disciplines such as the humanities, social sciences, natural sciences, health sciences, and engineering. While SDU’s main campus is in Odense, it also has campuses in other locations.   

Equal opportunity employment The University of Southern Denmark is an equal opportunity employer. We consider all qualified applicants without regard to race, colour, sex, gender identity, sexual orientation, religion, national origin, age, disability, pregnancy, or any other protected status.

The University of Southern Denmark wishes our staff to reflect the surrounding community and therefore encourages everyone, regardless of personal background, to apply for the position. SDU conducts research in critical technologies, which, due to the risk of unwanted knowledge transfer, are subject to a number of security measures. Therefore, based on information from open sources, background checks may be conducted on candidates for the position.

  How to apply Applications must be submitted electronically via the "Apply online" link provided in the job posting.

If you experience technical problems, please contact our email support.

 

The application deadline is February 28, 2027, at 11.59 PM/23.59 (CET/CEST)

The Danish Institute for Advanced Study (DIAS) and the Department of Green Technology at the University of Southern Denmark (SDU) invite applications for a tenure-track DIAS Fellow position at Assistant Professor level in Industrial Ecology and Data-Driven Sustainability Assessment, with a focus on input-output life cycle assessment methods and big data. Teaching obligations will be reduced compared to a standard assistant professorship at SDU, allowing more time for research and leadership activities.

Who are we looking for?

The position translates this ambition into a concrete research agenda, because many of the most pressing sustainability questions, such as how consumption in one country drives resource use, emissions and social conditions in another, or how a new technology changes environmental impacts across whole economies, cannot be answered within a single discipline. Industrial ecology addresses these questions by tracing material, energy and monetary flows through global supply chains, drawing on methods and data from engineering, economics and the natural and social sciences. Input-output analysis, built on big data covering production, trade, emissions and resource use and combined with life cycle assessment and material flow analysis, provides the quantitative framework for linking decisions about individual products, technologies and policies to their economy-wide consequences. The Fellow will build this capacity at SDU and use DIAS as a platform to work with researchers in fields such as health, food, energy, economics and political science on questions that cross disciplinary boundaries. Within this ambition, the specific profile is as follows.

We seek an early-career researcher who will advance quantitative sustainability assessment within industrial ecology by developing data-driven environmental-economic and systems models that link global production and consumption to environmental and socioeconomic outcomes. The role includes independent research, research-based teaching and supervision, interdisciplinary collaboration across DIAS and the Department, and development of competitive external funding proposals. Relevant research themes include:

·         environmental and material footprinting of global production and consumption systems;

·         development and application of environmentally extended input–output (EEIO) and multi-regional input–output (MRIO) models and databases, including hybrid physical–monetary systems and transparent, reproducible data workflows;

·         hybrid modelling that combines EEIO analysis with life cycle assessment (LCA), material flow analysis (MFA), econometrics or other quantitative methods;

·         applications to food and resource systems, healthcare systems and medical technologies, the circular economy, energy, infrastructure and other societal systems; and

·         scenario, structural decomposition, uncertainty and econometric analysis for sustainability transitions, policy and decision support.

·         Exhibit curiosity-driven research excellence, thinking beyond traditional boundaries.

·         Be fluent in English.

·         Show potential for attracting external research funding. Experience in applying for external funding and a strong international network are considered comparative advantages.

·         Have research publications that demonstrate their excellence and broad thinking.

The Department of Green Technology at SDU is a dynamic and interdisciplinary research environment focused on developing technologies and strategies for a sustainable future. Our research spans environmental chemistry, process engineering, life cycle thinking, and circular systems. We collaborate closely with industry and public stakeholders to ensure real-world impact and relevance.

This position will be affiliated with SDU Life Cycle Engineering (SDU LCE).

SDU Life Cycle Engineering

SDU LCE uses industrial ecology approaches to reduce environmental impacts and reconcile human development with environmental stewardship. We conduct holistic systems analyses and design studies to characterise and optimise engineering solutions over the long term, considering resource use, energy efficiency, climate and environmental impacts, and economic and socioeconomic performance. At SDU LCE, we develop and apply theory, methods and tools for material flow analysis (MFA), life cycle assessment (LCA), life cycle engineering, energy-system analysis and design, resource-criticality assessment, process integration and techno-economic assessment.

title: SMD Operators for a New Evening Shift
description:
Are you an experienced SMD Operator with a keen eye for quality, stable processes and precision-driven electronics manufacturing? Do you thrive in a technical environment where you take responsibility, work in a structured manner and actively contribute to a strong team? Then you could be our next experienced SMD Operator at NECAS A/S.

About the position

As an SMD Operator at NECAS, you will play a key role in the operation of our SMD lines – the heart of our electronics manufacturing. You will be responsible for setting up, monitoring and optimising processes, ensuring that production meets our high quality standards.

The electronics you help produce are used in everything from industrial and marine applications to defence and aerospace – industries where precision and reliability are essential.

You will become part of a highly skilled team and report to the Team Leader.

Your responsibilities

SMD line operation and preparation

  • Operate and monitor SMD equipment, including solder paste printer, SPI, pick-and-place, AOI and reflow oven

  • Prepare the line for production changeovers, including programmes, materials, feeder setup and documentation

  • Ensure stable operation in accordance with production plans and work instructions

  • Work with supporting processes such as the washing machine and stencil cleaner

Quality and inspection

  • Carry out process and quality inspections, including visual inspection and First Article Inspection

  • Analyse AOI results and respond to deviations

  • Ensure the correct handling of materials and components, including batch control, traceability and shelf life

  • Work in accordance with the IPC-A-610 standard (certification provided where required)

  • Record defects and deviations in the quality management system

Collaboration and continuous improvement

  • Ensure good communication and effective handovers between shifts

  • Share knowledge and support colleagues in their daily work

  • Contribute suggestions for improving processes and workflows

  • Maintain order and structure in the SMD area in accordance with 5S principles

About you

We are looking for a candidate who already has solid experience in SMD production and is able to work independently in a technically demanding role.

We expect you to:

  • Have a minimum of 3 years' experience with SMD equipment or electronics manufacturing

  • Be structured and able to maintain an overview, even during busy periods

  • Take responsibility and respond quickly when something deviates from the standard

  • Be a team player who contributes positively to the team

  • Have a technical understanding and an interest in working with advanced equipment

  • Language: good command of English, spoken and written

What we offer

At NECAS, you will become part of a growing company where quality and professional expertise are at the heart of what we do. You will receive:

  • A thorough introduction to our processes and equipment

  • Opportunities for relevant training and certifications, such as IPC-A-610

  • A strong team environment and an informal culture with a high level of professional expertise

  • A workplace in Støvring's newest industrial area, close to the E45 motorway

  • Competitive terms of employment, including pension and health insurance

About NECAS

NECAS is one of Denmark's leading EMS companies, manufacturing electronics for the industrial, marine/offshore, defence, aerospace and scientific sectors – industries where quality and precision are essential. The company currently has 62 employees.

We are one of the few EMS manufacturers in Denmark with AS9100 certification for the aerospace industry. At NECAS, you will become part of a company experiencing significant growth, where you can develop your professional skills and help push the boundaries of Danish electronics manufacturing.

As we say: Build for trust.

How to apply

The position will be filled as soon as possible. We are inviting candidates to interviews on an ongoing basis, so please send your application and CV as soon as possible. Please apply through our website at www.necas.com/karriere. We read all applications and will contact candidates we would like to get to know better.

If you have any questions, please contact Team Leader Mariana Surleac on +45 92 92 76 20.

title: Assistant Professor in Orthopaedic Surgery - Knee Surgery
description:
A position as Assistant Professor (35% time) is vacant at the Research Unit of Orthopaedic Surgery, the Department of Clinical Research, Faculty of Health Sciences, University of Southern Denmark.  The position is combined with an employment at Odense University Hospital.

The position is limited to 4 years.

The research unit

The Research Unit of Orthopaedic Surgery provides a dynamic and multidisciplinary research environment and is engaged in a broad range of research activities. Our research spans clinical and experimental as well as epidemiological research, including registry-based research and accident analysis.

Our team consists of both scientific and technical/administrative staff, including professors, postdoctoral researchers, PhD students, research nurses, secretaries and a laboratory technician.

We have extensive collaborations with other medical specialties and research groups, both nationally and internationally, fostering interdisciplinary research and knowledge exchange.

Research tasks

  • Serve as project lead for the REPLAN research project, with responsibility for its scientific direction, coordination, and overall progress. The REPLAN project investigates whether routine patellar resurfacing reduces patient dissatisfaction and knee pain compared with non-resurfacing in contemporary primary total knee arthroplasty. 

  • Supervise a PhD student, including providing scientific guidance and supporting the progress and completion of the PhD project.

  • Prepare and publish scientific manuscripts in peer-reviewed international journals and present research findings at national and international conferences.

Teaching tasks

  • Contribute to teaching medical students and clinical biomechanics students within orthopaedic surgery, with particular emphasis on knee surgery. 

Expectations and qualifications

The job involves research, professional development, research education, research-based teaching, including exams, supervision within the field of knee surgery. 

The candidate who is hired must complete a Lecturer Training Programme during the period of employment.

The assistant professor must have documented research experience within the area of knee arthroplasty. 

In addition, good cooperation skills are expected in order to further the development of research in the areas mentioned above, both interdisciplinary as well as nationally and internationally. International partners are an advantage, but not a requirement.

Research strategy for OUH and the Department of Clinical Research

The joint research strategy for the Department of Clinical Research and Odense University Hospital sets the direction for our shared research efforts in the years ahead. Rooted in the vision –We conduct research together to shape the patient care of the future – it focuses in particular on: cross-disciplinary research – with people at the centre; strong research environments – as drivers of development; and the research journey – from idea to impact. Further information on the joint research strategy of the Department of Clinical Research and Odense University Hospital is available here.

Further information

Further information about the position can be obtained from Head of Research at The Research Unit of Orthopaedic Surgery, Martin Lindberg-Larsen, e-mail: martin.lindberg-larsen@rsyd.dk, phone: +45 2521 3900 or Head of Department of Clinical Research, Rikke Leth-Larsen, e-mail: rllarsen@health.sdu.dk, phone: +45 6550 3477.

Application deadline

December 08, 2026, at 23.59 hrs. (CET/CEST).

Salary and terms of employment

The applicant will be employed in accordance with the agreement between the Ministry of Finance and AC (the Danish Confederation of Professional Associations).

The position as Assistant Professor is placed within salary steps 4–8 of the Danish state salary scale, depending on seniority. In addition, a centrally agreed assistant professor allowance is paid, and further qualification- and function-related allowances may be negotiated.

The work location will be at Odense University Hospital, J.B. Winsløws Vej 4, 5000 Odense C.   

Application

Applications must be submitted electronically using the link “Apply now” - see below.

We strongly recommend that you read How to apply for a position at SDU before you apply.

Only applications written in English will be accepted for evaluation.

The application must include (as PDF files) (please note that the application (the motivation letter) and CV must not exceed 10 MB in total):

  • a motivation letter

  • a detailed CV

  • degree certificates (MsC and Ph.D.-diploma)

  • a complete and numbered list of publications

  • 3 scientific peer-reviewed publications considered by the candidate as most important for this position. Please note that a copy of each publication must be attached as a pdf file.

    • It is permitted to merge copies of the selected publications into a single PDF file.

  • a teaching portfolio detailing the candidate’s prior teaching experience, teaching skills, and teaching philosophy

  • a research plan detailing the candidate’s ideas and plans for her/his future research work

  • An explanation other qualification relevant to the post

For technical issues, please contact: hcm-support@sdu.dk

Please note that all the above-mentioned information must be included in the application.  

Applications received after the deadline and/or incomplete applications will not be considered.

Assessment

Shortlisting will be used as part of the initial selection process. 

Assessment of shortlisted applications will be done under the existing Appointment Order for universities. Shortlisted applications will be assessed by an assessment committee. The committee may request additional information, and, if so, it is the responsibility of the applicant to provide the necessary material. 

When the assessment committee has submitted its report, the applicants will receive part of the evaluation that concerns themselves. 

References will be obtained for the preferred candidate from their current and previous employers. Applicants invited for interview should expect to complete a work-related personality assessment.

Living and working in Denmark

Foreign applicants will be offered Danish language training as part of the employment. 

The International Staff Office (ISO) at SDU provides a variety of services for new employees, guests and people who consider applying for a job at the University of Southern Denmark. 

The University wishes our staff to reflect the diversity of society and thus welcomes applications from all qualified candidates regardless of personal background.

title: Site Manager – new biogas plants in Denmark and abroad
description:
Site Manager – new biogas plants in Denmark and abroad

Bigadan is built by people with deep professional expertise and a shared ambition: to create the circular energy solutions of the future. We have been building biogas plants for more than 40 years, in Denmark and abroad, and the coming years are busy. We have expansion and greenfield projects lined up in Denmark and Scandinavia, plus support projects for our clients in Germany and the UK. That is why we are looking for an experienced Site Manager for our Projects team.

Anywhere from 10 to 50+ people from different contractors on site, all needing to deliver at the same time. You are the one holding it all together. And when you hand over, you leave behind a plant that produces biogas for decades.

The role

You lead the site day to day from ground-breaking through commissioning and handover to operations. The people on site are mainly contractors in civil, mechanical, electrical, piping and process works. You report formally to Head of Projects Luke Morris, while Head of Site Managers Stefan Wussow is your manager in day-to-day operations. You work closely with the individual Project Managers and the Site team.

You spend around 80% of your time on site and 20% in the office. Our construction site office and workshop are based in Husum, Germany. Ideally, we would like you to be based in southern Denmark near Kliplev or Husum, but as the role involves a lot of travel, we are recruiting across Denmark and northern Germany. Our projects are spread across Denmark and abroad, including Sweden, Germany, Finland and the UK.

We expect you to be ready for periods of 3–4 weeks living near the site. Employment can be in Denmark or in Germany.

What you do

Site leadership. You coordinate daily activities and contractor progress, plan access, deliveries and lifting operations, and solve problems before they become delays.

Safety. You lead site inspections and toolbox talks and approve risk assessments and method statements. You set the standard on site.

Quality and documentation. You make sure the work follows drawings and specifications, including welding, and keep track of inspections and documentation.

Handover. You manage punch lists and close-out, so we hand over a plant that works from day one.

What makes this role specific

With us, you are not building for a client you will never see again. We operate the plants ourselves afterwards, and our own colleagues will live with what you build for many years. You succeed in this role when you have led the next builds safely to completion, made the right decisions along the way, kept the budget on track, and made both the collaboration and the construction succeed.

We imagine that you:

• have a technical education, e.g. as a mechanical engineer, or a trade background (civil, mechanical or electrical) with hands-on experience

• have at least 5 years' experience as a site manager on industrial, energy, utility or process projects

• know civil, mechanical and electrical works and the health and safety rules on a construction site

• speak and write English and either Danish or German

Experience in biogas or anaerobic digestion is an advantage, but not a requirement. It is also an advantage if you hold a Danish construction safety coordinator certificate (AMK-B), first aid, knowledge of ATEX zones, or experience with welding coordination.

As a person, you are visible on site and make decisions when they need to be made. You can push back on a contractor and still have a good working relationship the next day.

We offer

A central role in a growing company, where you are involved from ground-breaking until the plant is running. You get a competitive salary, either mileage at the official Danish rates or a company van, accommodation and per diem on projects, pension and health insurance, ongoing training and support for relevant certifications. The position is full-time, starting 1 February or 1 March 2027.

About Bigadan

We develop, build, operate and own biogas plants and work across the entire value chain, from sourcing organic residues to producing energy, biogenic CO₂ and biofertiliser. We are around 200 colleagues and have built more than 40 biogas plants in Denmark and abroad.

Every day, we turn manure, food waste and other organic residues into products of value for the energy, agriculture and industrial sectors. This supports security of supply, makes better use of resources and returns nutrients to the soil.

Interested?

The application deadline is Wednesday 30 December 2026. We hold interviews on an ongoing basis, so please send your application and CV as soon as possible. If you have questions, please contact Head of Projects Luke Morris on +45 3073 6851 or lm@bigadan.dk.

title: Experienced farm team leaders for the harvest 2027
description:
Hyldetoftegaard A/S is looking for several experienced, reliable and motivated Farm Team Leaders to join our team for the 2027 fruit harvest season in Denmark, we employ approximately 200–220 employees.

We are looking for people with practical experience in agriculture, horticulture or fruit production who can lead and organize teams of fruit pickers and make sure that the daily work is well planned and carried out efficiently.

RECRUITMENT DAYS – CRAIOVA, ROMANIA – JANUARY 2027

RAMADA PLAZA CRAIOVA, Craiova, Romania

Recruitment dates:

·        Tuesday, 26 January 2027

·        Wednesday, 27 January 2027

Selected candidates will be invited to attend a short information meeting followed by individual employment interviews.

IMPORTANT – INVITATION ONLY

Attendance is strictly by individual invitation from Hyldetoftegaard A/S.

Only pre-selected candidates with a confirmed invitation will be admitted.

Unannounced visits and attendance without an invitation will be refused.

Applying does not guarantee an interview or an invitation.

English is the working language within the company.

YOUR MAIN RESPONSIBILITIES

·        Lead and organize a team of fruit pickers.

·        Plan and distribute the daily work among the workers.

·        Give clear instructions and make sure that tasks are understood.

·        Follow up on the team's daily work, progress and productivity.

·        Make sure that fruit picking is carried out efficiently and correctly.

·        Support the team and solve practical problems during the working day.

·        Register and report the team's daily harvest and output.

·        Keep simple and accurate records of workers, working hours and daily production.

·        Communicate daily information clearly to farm management.

·        Help ensure that safety, hygiene and company rules are followed.

ADMINISTRATIVE RESPONSIBILITIES

The Team Leaders will also have simple administrative responsibilities. You must be comfortable recording daily information and reporting it to management.

·        Register the team's daily fruit harvest/output.

·        Keep track of daily work and working hours.

·        Prepare simple daily reports.

·        Report relevant information and issues to farm management.

ENGLISH – REQUIRED

You must be able to communicate in English with management, understand information and handle everyday communication.

WHAT WE ARE LOOKING FOR

·        Previous experience as a team leader, supervisor, foreman or similar position.

·        Experience from agriculture, horticulture, fruit production or another relevant field.

·        Experience leading, motivating and organizing a team of workers.

·        Good communication and organizational skills.

·        Ability to take responsibility and work independently.

·        A positive and respectful approach to working with people from different countries.

·        Good English communication skills – required.

·        Good physical condition and willingness to work alongside the team when necessary.

WORKING PERIOD

The 2027 fruit harvest season runs from early May to mid-September or the end of October, depending on the harvest, we prefer you start in February and until Mid – end of October

The exact employment period will be agreed according to the farm's needs and your availability.

WORKING HOURS

·        Work normally starts at 05:00 or 06:00.

·        Approximately 6–7 working hours per day.

·        6 working days per week, with one changing day off.

·        Flexibility is required during busy periods of the harvest.

SALARY

Farm Team Leaders are employed on a fixed monthly salary.

The starting salary is a minimum of DKK 24.000.

The salary will be agreed according to qualifications, previous experience and the responsibilities of the position.

IBAN bank account:

You can only register one IBAN bank account in your own name for salary payments during your employment period.

ACCOMMODATION

Indoor accommodation is available on or near the farm, for the day’s price. Dkr.70,00 will be deducted from salary.

Shared kitchen, bathroom and laundry facilities. The company provides free access to a washing machine, tumble dryer, electricity, water, heating, internet, and cleaning products for the maintenance of the accommodation provided.

 TAX CARD AND HEALTH INSURANCE CARD

The company will apply for your tax card and health insurance card in accordance with your employment contract. These cards will be valid for the agreed employment period. If you are married, you must provide documentation of your marital status.

TAX DEDUCTIONS FOR FOREIGN EMPLOYEES

Foreign employees working temporarily in Denmark may be eligible for certain tax deductions, depending on their individual tax situation.

 Travel between your home country and Denmark

If you maintain your permanent home in your home country and your personal and financial ties remain there, you may be eligible for a deduction for travel between your home country and your workplace in Denmark. Eligibility depends on your Danish tax status. You must keep documentation of your journeys, such as tickets and receipts. The amount shown for 2026 is approximately DKK 6,000.

Double-household deduction

If your employment in Denmark is temporary and you maintain a home both in Denmark and in your home country, you may, under certain conditions, qualify for a deduction for additional household expenses. This may apply when your work requires you to live away from your permanent home.

To qualify, your employment must generally be temporary, and the distance between the two homes must make daily travel unreasonable. The deduction may be available for up to two years.

For 2026, the standard deduction for double housekeeping is DKK 400 per week without documentation. A higher deduction may be possible if you can document your actual expenses. The total deduction for food, accommodation and double housekeeping is subject to an annual maximum of DKK 34,400 for 2026. 

Important: These deductions are not automatic. You are responsible for checking whether you qualify and for entering the relevant deductions on your Danish tax assessment. Keep your documentation in case the Danish Tax Agency requests it.

TRANSPORT TO DENMARK

You must arrange and pay for your own transport to Denmark.

 If possible, bring your own car. A car can make your stay easier and more convenient, as you may need to travel between different farm locations and your accommodation in nearby houses. It will also give you more freedom to explore the local area.

TRACTOR DRIVING & FORKLIFT CERTIFICATE – ADVANTAGES, NOT REQUIREMENTS

These qualifications are wishes from the company and will be considered positively. However, our main priority is to employ good Team Leaders who can lead people, organize the daily work and take responsibility.

HOW TO APPLY:

If you wish to apply, send an email to job@hyldetoftegaard.dk and you will receive an application form. See more at www.hyldetoftegaard.dk

Applicants wishing to attend an employment interview in Craiova must submit their completed application form and a copy of their ID card in advance.

You will then receive a separate invitation, which must be brought to the interview together with documentation of your previous work experience, as outlined in the instructions

 Important – Application Feedback

Only qualified applicants will be contacted.

If you do not receive a response from the company within 14 days of submitting your application, please consider that your application has not been successful and that you have not been selected to proceed to the next stage of the recruitment process.

Thank you for your interest and understanding.

title: Hyldetoftegaard A/S is looking for experienced, motivated and reliable seasonal workers EU/EEA citizens to join our team for the berry harvest season 2027 in Denmark.
description:
Hyldetoftegaard A/S is looking for experienced, motivated and reliable seasonal fruit pickers from EUROPE only EU/EEA countries to join our team for the 2027 berry harvest season in Denmark.

At our farm, we grow strawberries, raspberries and blackberries

During the summer season, we employ approximately 200–220 workers.

Working period:

The season runs from early May to end of October, depending on the harvest.

We offer you a working contract for the period of more than 16 weeks.

·        We recruit on an ongoing basis, with start dates beginning in early May.

·        New employees start each week, with the final employees starting at the end of June.

·        We prefer candidates who are willing to work until the end of the season in October.

Experience:

We are looking for experienced fruit pickers. Previous experience with fruit picking or agricultural work is important.

Applications without information about previous experience will not be considered.

Your job:

·        Picking strawberries, raspberries and blackberries in greenhouses and tunnels.

·        The work is physically demanding and requires a good level of fitness.

·        You must be prepared to work outdoors and in different weather conditions.

 **********************************************************************************************************

 

RECRUITMENT DAYS – CRAIOVA, ROMANIA – JANUARY 2027

 

RAMADA PLAZA CRAIOVA, Craiova, Romania

Recruitment dates:

 

·        Tuesday, 26 January 2027

·        Wednesday, 27 January 2027

 

Selected candidates will be invited to attend a short information meeting followed by individual employment interviews.

 

IMPORTANT – INVITATION ONLY

 

Attendance is strictly by individual invitation from Hyldetoftegaard A/S.

Only pre-selected candidates with a confirmed invitation will be admitted.

Unannounced visits and attendance without an invitation will be refused.

Applying does not guarantee an interview or an invitation.

***************************************************************************************************************

 Working conditions:

·        Work starts at 05:00 or 06:00.

·        6–7 working hours per day.

·        6 working days per week, with one changing day off.

·        Physically demanding work outdoors and in greenhouses in different weather conditions.

What to bring:

Please remember to bring:

-         Sleeping bag – Towels and other personal necessities

-         Warm clothing

-         Practical work clothes

-         Boots and waterproof clothing

-         Even in good weather, plants can be very wet in the morning.

Payment and Compensation

·        Payment is based on piecework and/or hourly wages throughout the season, depending on the quantity and quality of your work.

·        You will be registered with the Danish Tax Agency (SKAT).

·        Your salary will be transferred directly to your IBAN bank account, and you will receive an official pay slip.

Holiday Allowance:

Will be paid to “FerieKonto” and you will get them according to Danish holidays rules, when you apply for them after the working period. This also applies to foreign employees who work in Denmark and are covered by Danish holiday rules. You generally earn 12.5% of your salary as holiday pay.

Requirements:

·        EU/EEA citizenship and a valid passport or ID.

·        Good physical condition.

·        Previous fruit-picking or farm experience.

·        Ability to follow Danish safety and hygiene rules.

·        Ability to understand a little English

Accommodation:

Accommodation (indoor) is available on or near the farm.

Reasonable rent D. kr. 70,00 pr. day will be deducted from your wages.

Shared kitchen with facilities, bathroom and laundry facilities, internet electricity, water, heating, internet, and cleaning products for the maintenance of the accommodation provided.

Tax and health card:

The company applies for your tax card and health insurance card in accordance with the employment contract. These are valid for the agreed employment period. If you are married, you must provide documentation of your marital status.

Tax Deductions for Foreign Employees

Foreign employees working temporarily in Denmark may, depending on their individual tax situation, be entitled to certain tax deductions.

Travel deduction between the home country and DenmarkIf you maintain your permanent home in your home country and your personal and financial interests remain there, you may be entitled to a tax deduction for transportation between your home country and your Danish workplace. This depends on your tax status in Denmark, and you must be able to document your journeys, for example by keeping tickets, receipts or other relevant documentation, around DKK 6.000 in 2026

Double housekeeping deductionIf your employment in Denmark is temporary and you maintain a home both in Denmark and in your home country, you may, under certain conditions, be entitled to a deduction for double housekeeping. This is intended for employees who have additional household expenses because their work requires them to live away from their permanent home.

To qualify, the employment must generally be temporary, and the distance between the two homes must be such that daily travel would not be reasonable. The deduction may be available for a maximum of two years.

For 2026, the standard deduction for double housekeeping is DKK 400 per week without documentation. A higher deduction may be possible if the actual expenses can be documented. The total deduction for food, accommodation and double housekeeping is subject to an annual maximum of DKK 34,400 in 2026.

Important: These deductions are not automatically granted. Each employee is responsible for checking whether they meet the conditions and for entering the relevant deductions on their Danish tax assessment. Documentation must be retained in case the Danish Tax Agency (Skattestyrelsen) requests it.

Transport to Denmark

You must arrange and pay for your own transport to Denmark.

Please bring your own car if possible. Having a car will make your stay much easier and more convenient, as you may need to travel between different farm locations and your accommodation in the nearby houses. It will also give you more freedom to get around and enjoy your time in the area.

HOW TO APPLY

If you wish to apply, send an email to job@hyldetoftegaard.dk and you will receive an application form.

See more: www.hyldetoftegaard.dk

Applicants wishing to attend an employment interview in Craiova must submit their completed application form and a copy of their ID card in advance.

You will then receive a separate invitation, which must be brought to the interview together with documentation of your previous work experience, as outlined in the instructions.

Important – Application Feedback

Only qualified applicants will be contacted.

If you do not receive a response from the company within 14 days of submitting your application, please consider that your application has not been successful and that you have not been selected to proceed to the next stage of the recruitment process.

Thank you for your interest and understanding.

title: Research Assistant followed by a Double Degree PhD position in Urban Design and Pedestrian Experience with AI and VR
employer: KU - SCIENCE - IGN frb campus omr. 3
description:
Department of Geosciences and Natural Resource Management, Faculty of SCIENCE, University of Copenhagen Within the European Union’s Horizon Europe research and innovation programme under the Marie Skłodowska-Curie Action (MSCA), University of Copenhagen is offering a 1-year Research Assistant (RA) position starting 1 April 2027 (or as soon as possible thereafter), which then leads to a 3-year PhD fellowship for a Doctoral Candidate (DC). The combined position is part of the research project STEP-UP (Safe, Thriving, and Engaged Pedestrians in Urban Public Spaces), which is funded by the European Union’s Marie Skłodowska-Curie Actions (MSCA), Doctoral Networks (DN), Call: HORIZON-MSCA-2025-DN-01. The STEP-UP network supports 10 PhD Candidates in investigating pedestrian behaviour and mobility in urban environments. The 10 PhD projects are closely linked, contributing complementary perspectives to a shared research agenda in three areas: individual and interpersonal aspects of pedestrian behaviour, environmental and infrastructural barriers to walking, and interactions between pedestrians and other road users. The aim is to improve the understanding of pedestrian mobility and support the development of safer and more inclusive urban public spaces. STEP-UP brings together academic and non-academic partners to train 10 doctoral candidates through an international Joint Doctorate programme. The candidates benefit from joint supervision by researchers at partner institutions, an integrated doctoral training programme, and opportunities for interdisciplinary and cross-sectoral collaboration, including research secondments at partner organisations. In addition to specialised scientific knowledge, they develop transferable skills in areas such as research communication and dissemination. The programme prepares them for careers in research and other fields related to transport and urban development. For a description of the STEP-UP project and descriptions of all 10 PhD positions, please visit the STEP-UP project’s website https://www.project-stepup.eu/ STEP-UP is based on 4-year double PhD degree programs. This means that the successful applicant will also be enrolled in a partner university’s PhD programme. Job and project description The RA position will entail carrying out a literature review of the research field, identifying current research gaps, and preparing for data collection. The PhD position will entail carrying out the research activities of the research project as described below. Your key tasks as a PhD fellow at the Faculty of SCIENCE are to:
  • Conduct an independent research project under supervision.
  • Complete PhD courses or other equivalent education corresponding to approximately 30 ECTS points.
  • Participate in active research environments including a mandatory stay for a minimum of 12 months at the partner university (see below for further details).
  • Contribute to teaching or other types of dissemination related to your PhD project (e.g., at conferences, meetings, etc.)
  • Write a PhD thesis on the grounds of your project
About the research project The project “Urban space transformation projects for improved and inclusive walkability”. will investigate how planning and design approaches applied in urban space transformation projects impact pedestrians’ behaviour and perceived safety and accessibility (walkability). Urban transformation projects are increasingly proposed to respond to the evolving needs of contemporary cities. Combining urban planning and transport engineering is essential, as planning shapes the spatial and social context of urban spaces while transport engineering ensures safe, efficient and accessible movement. The PhD project will: (1) collect data on goals and practices of urban space transformation projects; pedestrian pedestrians’ behaviours, preferences and perceptions of walkability in relation to the transformation interventions; (2) identify walkability indicators across diverse groups of pedestrians; (3) comprehensively evaluate pedestrians’ perceived impacts of current transformations for enhanced liveability and pedestrianisation; and (4) develop a methodological framework for local adaptation and upscaling of approaches for enhanced perceived walkability. Partner university: National Technical University of Athens (NTUA) Planned secondments at NTUA: M16–M24 and M37–M48. Pricipal supervisor: Assoc. Prof. Trine Agervig Carstensen, University of Copenhagen, email: tac@ign.ku.dk. Co-supervisor: Prof. Konstantinos Kepaptsoglou, National Technical University of Athens (NTUA), email: kkepap@central.ntua.gr Place of employment The primary place of employment will be Department of Geosciences and Natural Resource Management, Faculty of SCIENCE, University of Copenhagen. We offer creative and stimulating working conditions in dynamic and international research environment. Our research facilities include modern laboratories and state-of-the-art hardware and software. More information on the department can be found here: https://ign.ku.dk/english/ During the PhD programme of research the candidate will be on a secondment for minimum 12 months in total at the partner university. Required qualifications As an applicant you must have:
  • To be eligible for the PhD programme at UCPH, you must have completed a degree programme, equivalent to a Danish master’s degree (180 ECTS/3 FTE BSc + 120 ECTS/2 FTE MSc) related to the subject area of the project, e.g. Urban Planning, Geography, Civil Engineering, Psychology, Architecture, Landscape Architecture, Sociology, or related-disciplines. For information of eligibility of completed programmes, see General assessments for specific countries and Assessment database.
  • To be eligible for the PhD programme at the National University of Athens, you are required to fulfil the requirements described here: https://eur02.safelinks.protection.outlook.com/?url=https%3A%2F%2Fwww.survey.ntua.gr%2Fen%2Fstudies%2Fpostgraduate%2Fdoctoral-studies&data=05%7C02%7Ctac%40ign.ku.dk%7Ce197702553f44a00a12308df44a25d10%7Ca3927f91cda14696af898c9f1ceffa91%7C0%7C0%7C639305136264965933%7CUnknown%7CTWFpbGZsb3d8eyJFbXB0eU1hcGkiOnRydWUsIlYiOiIwLjAuMDAwMCIsIlAiOiJXaW4zMiIsIkFOIjoiTWFpbCIsIldUIjoyfQ%3D%3D%7C0%7C%7C%7C&sdata=62PInKwPpyGrwa3VViUOFLlXisPlz4b7rgs6kdWwhNI%3D&reserved=0
  • Fluency in English and excellent communications skills.
Applicants will also be required to meet the European Commission’s MSCA Doctoral Network eligibility criteria, notably:
  • Mobility Rule - Applicants can be of any nationality and must not have resided or carried out their main activity (work, studies, etc.) in Denmark for more than 12 months in the 36 months immediately before the start of their employment at UCPH. Compulsory national service, short stays such as holidays, and time spent as part of a procedure for obtaining refugee status under the Geneva Convention are not considered.
  • Doctoral Candidate requirement – the applicant must not be in possession of a doctoral degree at the first day of the employment. Researchers who have successfully defended their doctoral thesis, but who have not yet been awarded the doctoral degree are not eligible.
Please note that you will only be considered for the position if you fulfil both above eligibility criteria. Who are we looking for? We are looking for candidates within the field(s) of spatial, engineering, or behavioural sciences. Applicants can have a background in Urban and Regional Planning, Geography, Civil Engineering, Architecture, Landscape Architecture, Psychology, Sociology, or related disciplines. The following experiences and skills will be emphasised. Applicants are encouraged to provide relevant details and supporting evidence, where applicable:
  • Urban design / urban planning
  • Human-environment interactions
  • Qualitative case study methods
  • Data analysis / statistical analysis
Personal attributes that are desirable:
  • Strong motivation for high-quality research
  • Collaborative spirit
  • Systematic approach to research
  • Attention to detail
Key criteria for the assessment of applicants
  • Professional qualifications relevant to the PhD project
  • Relevance of studies, coursework, and thesis
  • Relevant work experience (if any)
  • Publications (if any)
  • The grade point average achieved
  • Other professional activities
  • Language skills
  • Quality and relevance of project proposal
  • The successful applicant is also required to be enterprising and to possess good interpersonal skills
Terms of employment The arrangement concerns two separate fixed-term positions: initially as a Research Assistant, leading towards an appointment as a PhD fellow. The respective durations of the two positions are 1 year and 3 years. The position as a PhD fellow is contingent upon the successful enrolment of a suitable candidate in the PhD School at the University of Copenhagen, as well as satisfactory completion of the Research Assistant period. These assessments will be carried out 3-6 months prior to the expiry of the Research Assistant contract. The start date is 1 April 2027 or as soon as possible thereafter. The PhD study must be completed in accordance with The Ministerial Order on the PhD programme (2013) and the faculty’s rules on achieving the degree. Salary, pension and terms of employment are in accordance with the requirements from the European Commission related to the MSCA programme and the agreement between the Ministry of Taxation and The Danish Confederation of Professional Associations on Academics in the State. Depending on seniority, the monthly salary starts at approximately 31,850 DKK/roughly 4,260 EUR (August 2026 level). Depending on qualifications, a supplement may be negotiated. The employer will pay an additional 18.07 % to your pension fund. Application and assessment procedure Your application, written in English, must be submitted electronically by clicking “Apply now” below and must include the following documents in PDF format:
  • Motivation letter of application (max. one page)
  • A project proposal (max 5 pages where the candidate presents a proposal on how they wish to approach their project including theory and methods)
  • CV incl. education, experience, language skills, publication list (if any), and other skills relevant for the position
  • Certified copy of original master’s diploma and transcript of records in the original language, including an authorised English translation if issued in other language than English or Danish. If not completed, a certified/signed copy of a recent transcript of records or a written statement from the institution or supervisor is accepted. As a prerequisite for a PhD position employment, you must have completed a degree programme, equivalent to a Danish master’s degree (180 ECTS/3 FTE BSc + 120 ECTS/2 FTE MSc) related to the subject area of the project. For information of eligibility of completed programmes, see General assessments for specific countries and Assessment database. Please note that we might ask you to obtain an assessment of your education performed by the Ministry of Higher Education and Science. Applicants with a master´s degree from abroad should also enclose a short description of the grading scale used. Certified copy of original bachelor’s diploma and transcript of records in the original language, including an authorised English translation if issued in other language than English or Danish. If the applicant has completed a combined bachelor’s and master’s education (e.g. 5-year combined master’s), the applicant should submit the combined diploma, transcript of records, and authorised English translations if issued in other language than English or Danish.
  • Language diplomas or language test results (if any)
The deadline for applications is 20 December 2026, at 23.59pm CET. We reserve the right not to consider material received after the deadline, and not to consider applications that do not live up to the abovementioned requirements. The further process After the expiry of the deadline for applications, the authorised recruitment manager selects applicants for assessment on the advice of the hiring committee. All applicants are then immediately notified whether their application has been passed for assessment by an unbiased assessor. The assessor makes a non-prioritised assessment of the academic qualifications and experience with respect to the above-mentioned area of research, techniques, skills and other requirements listed in the advertisement. Once the assessment work has been completed, each applicant can comment on the part of the assessment that relates to him/herself. The applicant will be assessed according to the Ministerial Order no. 242 of 13 March 2012 on the Appointment of Academic Staff at Universities. You may read about the recruitment process at http://employment.ku.dk/faculty/recruitment-process/ For more information on working and living in Denmark visit http://ism.ku.dk (International Staff Mobility) and https://www.workindenmark.dk. Interviews are expected to take place in the beginning of February 2027. Questions For specific information about the PhD position, please contact the principal supervisor, Trine Agervig Carstensen. The University of Copenhagen wishes to reflect the diversity of society and encourages all qualified candidates to apply regardless of personal background.

title: Postdoctoral Researcher in Human Skin Biology and Wound Healing
description:
Postdoctoral Researcher in Human Skin Biology and Wound Healing Department of Biology, Faculty of Science, University of Copenhagen The Department of Biology at the University of Copenhagen invites applications for a postdoctoral researcher in human skin biology and wound healing. The position is part of a newly established research group investigating how cells coordinate their behaviour to maintain and repair tissues. The position is fully funded for at least 2 years, with the possibility of extension, through generous funding from the LEO Foundation. The earliest possible start date is 1 April 2027. Please clearly state your availability and preferred start date in your cover letter. Information about the Department of Biology is available at https://www1.bio.ku.dk/english/. Information about the specific research section you will be affiliated with is available at https://www1.bio.ku.dk/english/research/cbp/. Project overview The overarching aim is to develop strategies to help people with slow- or non-healing wounds. This project investigates how planar cell polarity (PCP)—the coordinated orientation of cells within a tissue—contributes to human skin organization and wound repair. Although PCP signaling is essential for tissue organization across many organisms, its role in human epidermis remains poorly understood. You will establish reconstructed human epidermis (RHE) as an experimental model to investigate PCP signaling in human skin, then use advanced fluorescence microscopy to characterize PCP clusters, their polarization, and how they change during wound repair and in response to other stressors. The project bridges fundamental questions in cell and developmental biology with potential long-term applications in regenerative medicine and skin repair. It is supported by collaborators with expertise in RHE development and by access to confocal and advanced microscopy, including SIM, TIRF, and STED. The project provides a clear starting point and room to shape the research questions as findings emerge. In your cover letter, please clearly describe what interests you about the project and what related research questions you would be excited to explore. Your role We are seeking a motivated, technically skilled, and scientifically independent postdoctoral researcher to play a central role in establishing this research programme. As one of the first members of a newly established research group, you will have an exceptional opportunity to shape its experimental approaches, contribute to its scientific direction, and help build a collaborative, ambitious research environment. Your primary responsibility will be to establish and optimize experimental systems to investigate PCP signaling in reconstructed human epidermis. You will work closely with the PI while taking substantial ownership of day-to-day experimental development and execution of the project. Your responsibilities will include:
  • Establish and optimize robust, reproducible assays with mature, stratified RHE cultures.
  • Develop and optimize immunostaining, advanced microscopy, and quantitative imaging workflows.
  • Analyze and interpret experimental data, contributing scientific ideas, and identifying promising new research directions.
  • Prepare manuscripts for publication in peer-reviewed journals and presenting findings at local and international conferences.
  • Contribute to the development of a supportive, collaborative, and scientifically rigorous lab environment.
  • Help train and supervise students or other researchers as the group expands.
Profile We are seeking a curious and proactive researcher who can take ownership of their experiments while collaborating constructively with the project team. You do not need experience with every method listed below; training and collaboration will help you develop the techniques needed for the project. Essential experience and skills:
  • PhD in cell biology, developmental biology, skin biology, molecular biology, tissue engineering, biophysics, or a closely related field by the time of appointment.
  • Extensive hands-on experience in mammalian cell culture, with demonstrated ability to independently establish, optimize, and troubleshoot experimental protocols.
  • Demonstrated experience in fluorescence microscopy and immunofluorescence staining.
  • Evidence of scientific independence, initiative, and the ability to advance an experimental research project, including strong organizational skills.
  • A solid publication record appropriate for your career stage.
  • Excellent written and spoken English skills.
In the cover letter, you are encouraged to highlight an example of experimental independence, including situations in which you have established or substantially improved an experimental method, solved a challenging technical problem, or independently advanced a research project. Desirable experience and skills:
  • Experience with human keratinocyte culture, reconstructed human epidermis, organotypic skin cultures, or other 3D epithelial models.
  • Experience establishing new experimental model systems or developing and optimizing complex cell-culture protocols.
  • Experience with quantitative image analysis using Fiji/ImageJ, Python, or other comparable computational tools.
  • Experience with molecular perturbation techniques, including CRISPR/Cas9, RNA interference, and genetic manipulation of mammalian cells.
  • Experience with confocal microscopy or an advanced imaging technique such as SIM, TIRF, or STED.
  • Experience mentoring or supervising students or junior researchers.
Research shows that women and other underrepresented groups often hesitate to apply unless they meet every requirement. If you are excited about this position and believe you can contribute, we strongly encourage you to apply, even if your experience does not perfectly match every point. We value curiosity, motivation, and the potential and willingness to learn. What we offer
  • An opportunity to join a newly established research group and meaningfully contribute to its scientific development.
  • A central role in an ambitious, externally funded research project that addresses fundamental and medically relevant questions.
  • Substantial scientific independence and opportunities to develop novel experimental approaches.
  • Close scientific interaction with the PI and opportunities to shape future research directions.
  • Access to the research infrastructure and collaborative environment at the University of Copenhagen.
  • Opportunities for international collaboration, conference participation, publication, and professional development.
The position offers an excellent opportunity for a researcher seeking to develop greater scientific independence and strengthen their qualifications for a future academic or research leadership career. Terms of employment The average weekly working hours are 37 hours. The place of employment is at the Department of Biology, Section for Cell Biology and Physiology, University of Copenhagen. Salary, pension and other conditions of employment are set in accordance with the Agreement between the Ministry of Taxation and AC (Danish Confederation of Professional Associations) or other relevant organisation. Currently, the monthly salary starts at 35,000 DKK/approx. 4,700 EUR (October 2021 level). Depending on qualifications, a supplement may be negotiated. The employer will pay an additional 17.1 % to your pension fund. Foreign and Danish applicants may be eligible for tax reductions, if they hold a PhD degree and have not lived in Denmark the last 10 years. The position is covered by the Job Structure for Academic Staff at Universities 2020. Questions For further information, please contact PI: Silas Boye Nissen; boye.nissen@bio.ku.dk. Foreign applicants may find this link useful: www.ism.ku.dk (International Staff Mobility). Application procedure Your online application must be submitted in English by clicking ‘Apply now’ below. Furthermore, your application must include the following documents/attachments – all in PDF format:
  1. Motivated letter of application (max. one page).
  2. CV incl. education, work/research experience, and other skills/experience relevant for the position (see above).
  3. A certified/signed copy of a) PhD certificate and b) Master of Science certificate. If the PhD is not completed, a written statement from the supervisor will do.
  4. List of peer-reviewed publications.
Deadline for applications: December 31, 2026, 23:59 CET We reserve the right not to consider material received after the deadline, and not to consider applications that do not live up to the abovementioned requirements. The further process After the expiry of the deadline for applications, the authorized recruitment manager selects applicants for assessment on the advice of the hiring committee. All applicants are then immediately notified whether their application has been passed for assessment by an unbiased assessor. Once the assessment work has been completed each applicant has the opportunity to comment on the part of the assessment that relates to the applicant him/herself. You can read about the recruitment process at http://employment.ku.dk/faculty/recruitment-process/ The applicant will be assessed according to the Ministerial Order no. 242 of 13 March 2012 on the Appointment of Academic Staff at Universities. The University of Copenhagen wishes to reflect the diversity of society and encourage all qualified candidates to apply regardless of personal background.

title: RF Systems Architect
description:
Description & Expectation

Quadsat is looking for an experienced RF Systems Architect to join the RF team working on SpectraLoc, our defense product for detection, analysis, and geolocation of RF emitters.

This role will focus on RF front-end architecture, coherent receiver design, RF chain optimization, PCB design and layout, measurement integrity, and the continued productization of SpectraLoc. You will help strengthen the RF hardware foundation needed for robust product performance, certification readiness, and future next-generation RF architectures.

SpectraLoc combines RF sensing payloads, drone-based operations, mission control software, signal processing, geolocation algorithms, and operator-facing workflows into one integrated product. You will work closely with engineers spanning from RF, DSP, software, embedded, and FPGA specialist, with your primary focus being to improve RF system quality, hardware robustness, and the measurement integrity of the sensing chain.

For this role it is a requirement that you can confirm that you are eligible to be security cleared by the Danish Defense Intelligence Service.

Responsibilities:

Your main responsibility will be to develop, improve, and mature RF hardware and RF system architectures that support reliable RF sensing, geolocation, and future coherent receiver capabilities.

You will:

  • Design, develop, and optimize RF front-end architectures for RF sensing and geolocation applications.
  • Contribute to coherent receiver design, multi-channel RF architectures, and future direction-finding capabilities based on phase-coherent RF measurements.
  • Design and improve RF chains, including filtering, amplification, frequency conversion, gain distribution, dynamic range, noise figure, linearity, and sensitivity trade-offs.
  • Support PCB design and layout for RF circuits, including component selection, schematic design, layout review, signal integrity, grounding, shielding, and manufacturability.
  • Improve measurement integrity across the RF sensing chain by identifying and reducing sources of uncertainty, drift, phase error, loss, interference, leakage, and calibration sensitivity.
  • Plan and perform RF measurements, verification, and troubleshooting using relevant RF test equipment such as spectrum analysers, VNAs, signal generators, power meters, and related tools.
  • Work with DSP and software engineers to ensure that RF hardware behavior, calibration data, and system limitations are understood and properly reflected in algorithm development and product performance.
  • Support product robustness, certification readiness, and design-for-manufacturing activities by improving RF hardware quality, documentation, repeatability, and testability.
  • Provide technical leadership within RF systems and hardware, helping raise the quality of Quadsat’s RF design, validation methodology, and overall sensing performance.

Knowledge & Skills:

We envision that you have a bachelor’s or master’s degree in Electrical Engineering, RF Engineering, Microwave Engineering, Physics, or a related technical field, combined with strong practical experience in RF hardware development for RF sensing, SDR, radar, electronic warfare, SATCOM, aerospace, telecom, test and measurement, or other advanced RF systems.

More important than the exact degree is that you have hands-on experience designing, validating, and improving RF systems where measurement quality, robustness, and system performance matter.

In addition, you bring:

  • Strong practical experience with RF front-end design, RF chain architecture, and RF hardware development.
  • Experience with RF circuit design and PCB design/layout for high-frequency systems.
  • Solid understanding of RF system trade-offs, including gain, noise figure, dynamic range, linearity, filtering, frequency conversion, phase noise, spurious signals, leakage, and sensitivity.
  • Practical experience with RF measurement, verification, debugging, and calibration using professional RF test equipment.
  • Understanding of coherent RF systems, including phase stability, synchronization, channel matching, LO distribution, timing effects, and calibration considerations.
  • Familiarity with antenna interfaces, propagation effects, polarization, multipath, and how RF hardware behavior affects sensing and geolocation performance.
  • Ability to define test methods, performance metrics, acceptance criteria, and validation approaches for RF hardware and RF sensing systems.
  • Experience collaborating with DSP, software, embedded, FPGA, mechanical, robotics, and product teams to turn RF hardware concepts into robust product capabilities.
  • A proactive mindset, strong ownership, and the ability to work independently while staying aligned with broader product and engineering priorities.

It would be highly advantageous if you also have experience with electronic warfare, radar systems, SIGINT, RF surveillance, phased arrays, coherent multi-channel receivers, interferometry, monopulse tracking, beamforming, calibration of RF sensing systems, MIL-STD certification, environmental robustness, SDR platforms, or transitioning RF hardware from prototype into production.

Our Dynamic Work Environment:

Quadsat is at an exciting stage of our growth journey where you can make a meaningful impact with your work, and directly influence the development of advanced solutions. You will join a diverse team of innovative colleagues who are passionate about working with new technology development. Our work environment is characterised by a high degree of openness, a flat management structure, and a strong sense of community where we work closely together on tasks.

You will be part of a driven engineering team across software, RF, robotics, and product development, with opportunities for professional growth, increased responsibility, and close involvement in real product innovation. We value initiative, collaboration, high-quality engineering, and people who want their work to matter beyond the codebase.

Contact and Questions:

This hiring is being managed in collaboration with our external recruitment partner, ESBEES. For questions reach out to Søren Bøge Sørensen by mail: sbs@esbeesheadhunting.com or by phone: +45 20 27 46 66.
